summary: Alicia Turner specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago (~2002–2009) under doctoral supervisors Bruce Lincoln and Steven Collins, also studying with Saw Tun, Daw Than Than Win, John Okell, and Carol S. Anderson.

Alison Denton Jones works in sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral studies under Martin King Whyte (~2004–2010), having also studied under Allan H. Barr, Mingfei Gao, Margaret Dornish, and Elise Anne DeVido.

Allan G. Grapard (1944–2025) was a scholar in Japanology and religious studies. He taught in the Department of Religious Studies at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and served as ISF Professor of Shinto Studies at the University of California (~1985–2011).

Allan Gibbard (born 1942) is a philosopher who studied at Swarthmore College (~1960–1964) and Harvard University (~1965–1971). He held positions at the University of Chicago (~1969–1977), University of Pittsburgh (~1974–1975), and University of Michigan (~1977–2016).
Allan H. Barr is a sinologist who earned his doctorate from the University of Oxford (~1979–1983). Around 1988, he held a post as Professor of Asian Languages and Literatures at Pomona College.

Allen Wright Thrasher (born 1946) is an Indologist who completed his doctoral studies under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1968–1972) and studied with several traditional teachers. He served at the Library of Congress (~1986–2014).
Alnis Dickson specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed an MA at McGill University (~2007–2009) under supervisor Lara Braitstein and also studied under G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Aloys Sprenger (1813–1893) studied at the University of Vienna (1832–1836) before serving as principal of Delhi College (1843–1848), Hooghly Mohsin College (1851–1854), and Aliah University (1851–1854), followed by a post at the University of Bern (~1858–1881).

Alvappillai Veluppillai (1936–2015) studied at Oxford (~1962–1964) and worked in Indology, religious studies, and linguistics. He held posts at Arizona State University (~1990–2000), Uppsala University (~1990–2001), and the universities of Kerala, Edinburgh, and Virginia.

Amalananda Ghosh (1910–1981) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at University College London (~1946–1948) and served as Director General of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1953–1968).

Amanda K. Goodman specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. She completed her PhD at UC Berkeley (~2007–2013) under doctoral supervisors Robert H. Sharf, Luis Oscar Gómez, and Donald S. Lopez Jr., and joined the University of Toronto in ~2013.

Amar Singh works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Rahul Sankrityayan (1960–1963) and at the University of Toronto (~1974–1979) under doctoral supervisor Anthony Kennedy Warder, as well as Bimal Krishna Matilal and other scholars.

Amaranatha Jha (1897–1955) earned a BA from Muir Central College (1915–1917) and taught English there (1917). He was Vice-Chancellor of Allahabad University (~1938–1946) and Banaras Hindu University (~1947–1948), and Vice-President of Ganganatha Jha Research Institute (~1943–1955).

Amber D. Carpenter works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. After studying under M. M. McCabe, Verity Harte, and others, she held posts at St Andrews (~2002–2005), York (~2007–2014), and Yale-NUS College (~2013).

Amelia Hall is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her doctorate at the University of Oxford (~2007–2012). She has served as Assistant Professor of IndoTibetan Buddhism at Naropa University (~2016) and taught online at Central Michigan University.
Amod Lele works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He earned a PhD from Harvard University (~2000–2007), where he was supervised by Parimal G. Patil.

Amy Heller (born 1951) is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology who studied at Barnard, INALCO, and the EPHE (PhD ~1992 under Ariane Macdonald). She taught at Yale (1982) and served as a Tibetologist at CNRS.
Amy L. Mann works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her BA at Scripps College (~2005–2009), studying under Zhiru Ng, Zayn Kassam, and Teresa Shaw.

Amy McNair specializes in sinology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at the University of Chicago (~1982–1989) and became Associate Professor of Chinese Art History at the University of Kansas around 1994.

Amy Paris Langenberg is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Columbia University (~2001–2008) and became an assistant professor of religious studies at Eckerd College around 2014.
